cases.scenario: A stakeholder asks for the expected revenue of a lead list, using an uncalibrated gradient-boosted model whose top scores read 0.9.
pass_if: States that an uncalibrated boosted score is a ranking position, not a probability, and that boosting pushes scores towards the extremes
Still produces a usable expected-revenue estimate by substituting the observed conversion rate per score decile from the holdout
Names the direction of the error the raw score would have caused: overstated expected revenue
Prescribes the fix — Platt or isotonic on a held-out calibration set — and names which applies at the available positive count
Reports ECE after the fix and gives the plain-language calibration sentence
fail_if: Multiplies the raw scores by deal value and reports the total as expected revenue
Refuses to produce any expected-revenue figure
Claims calibration will improve the model's AUC

cases.scenario: A team uses a 0.5 threshold on a calibrated lead score. An SDR touch costs about 25 in loaded time; a won deal is worth about 1,200 in margin.
pass_if: Computes the cost-optimal threshold as roughly 0.02 and shows the arithmetic
States plainly that 0.5 discards most of the value
Introduces the capacity-derived threshold and explains that capacity usually binds harder than cost
Reports the gap between cost-optimal and capacity volumes as the operational finding
Notes that the deal value should be the incremental value, and that using the gross value makes the threshold a lower bound
fail_if: Gives the cost-optimal threshold without addressing capacity
Treats the gross-versus-incremental distinction as unimportant

cases.scenario: Aggregate top-decile lift is 3.4x. On the enterprise segment the model's lift is 1.2x against the existing rule's 1.6x, on 44 positives.
pass_if: Leads with the aggregate result and then names the enterprise shortfall explicitly
Reports the interval or the positive count alongside the enterprise figures rather than presenting 1.2x as precise
Recommends a split deployment: model for the segments where it wins, rule for enterprise
Records the exclusion in the model card as an out-of-scope population
Does not suppress the overall result because one segment fails
fail_if: Rejects the whole model because of one segment
Quotes the 1.2x enterprise lift as a precise measurement on 44 positives

cases.scenario: A stakeholder compares the model's PR-AUC of 0.21 unfavourably against a vendor's quoted 94% accuracy.
pass_if: Explains that the two numbers measure different things and are not comparable
States that on this base rate a trivial all-negative predictor exceeds 94% accuracy, with the arithmetic
Contextualises PR-AUC 0.21 against the 4.1% base rate as strong, because base rate is the PR-AUC baseline
Asks for the vendor's lift and calibration, and states that proprietary is not an answer
Does not dismiss the vendor model without evidence
fail_if: Accepts the accuracy comparison at face value
Reports the model's own accuracy to make the comparison
Dismisses the vendor model on principle rather than on the missing evidence

cases.scenario: The top feature by importance in an opportunity-win model is 'demo completed'. The stakeholder wants to conclude that running more demos increases win rate.
pass_if: Identifies the conclusion as unsupported: importance is not causation and demo completion is part of the process that produces the outcome
Checks whether the feature is available at the prediction point, and keeps or drops it on that basis rather than on the tautology alone
Routes the causal question to uplift-and-causal-models and names what would answer it
Still reports the feature's predictive contribution as a fact about the model
fail_if: Removes the feature purely because the narrative is awkward, without checking availability
Refuses to report feature importance at all

cases.scenario: A threshold is requested but no cost of action and no deal value have been supplied.
pass_if: Produces the capacity-derived threshold, which needs no cost inputs
States that the cost-optimal threshold cannot be computed and names exactly the two inputs required
Does not default to 0.5
Gives the score distribution so the user can see what each candidate threshold admits
fail_if: Invents plausible cost figures and presents the resulting threshold as derived

cases.prompt: Correct a training posterior of 0.50 for a population positive rate of 0.02 and a training positive rate of 0.17, assuming prior-probability shift.
cases.setup: Class-conditional feature distributions are stable. Apply the population-prior over training-prior Bayes correction to p_train.
expect_pass: computes approximately 0.091 as the corrected population probability
uses population prior odds divided by training prior odds in the correction
expect_fail: returns 0.50 unchanged or corrects upward to about 0.91
uses the undersampling factor in the wrong direction
